project._uiFrameworkNote: React 18/19 + Tailwind v4. globals.css is a shadcn-shaped token export, so component variant vocabulary follows shadcn naming.

Input._note: Code implemented, CI-bound, and now RENDERED and visually verified in Storybook across all five states in both modes. Still draft: promotion to stable is storybook-chromatic-builder's call and there is no Chromatic baseline. Rendering caught a real bug (see the cn/tailwind-merge fix) and disproved part of the focus-ring rationale.

Accordion._note: Implemented 9 Aug 2026. Figma models a SINGLE item; an Accordion is a group, so code takes items[] and openIds[] (an array, because several sections may be open at once, which the Figma State enum cannot express). The map types State as closed|open and Disabled as false|true string unions; both emitted as real booleans since a stringly-typed boolean is a Figma artefact not an API. Triggers are wrapped in headings for heading navigation - the difference from Collapsible. No focus token is recorded on this set; the shared ring treatment is asserted.

Alert._note: Implemented 9 Aug 2026 from LIVE BINDINGS. Both open questions settled. WARNING IS HALF-REBOUND IN FIGMA: title = warning-muted-foreground but description = plain warning; one of the two 3.07:1 nodes was fixed and the other missed. Code applies warning-muted-foreground to BOTH, because shipping a known contrast failure to match a half-finished rebind would be transcribing a bug. Success rebound both; Info deliberately neither (it passed at 4.82/4.88). Destructive has NO surface fill bound at all - the description fill card was reporting an unbound literal.

Alert Dialog._note: Implemented 9 Aug 2026. Two deliberate differences from Dialog, both accessibility decisions: the backdrop does NOT dismiss (a decision dismissed by misclick is how people lose data; Escape still cancels), and description is REQUIRED by the type. Initial focus goes to Cancel so a reflexive Enter takes the safe path. No slots on purpose - a slot would let a caller turn it back into a Dialog. This component binds card-foreground, which is the CORRECT pairing for a card fill; Dialog/Drawer/Sheet bind plain foreground on the same fill.

Avatar._note: Implemented 9 Aug 2026. UNBLOCKED BY A CORRECTION, not new information: it had been flagged as carrying pre-rebind stale tokens, but the detection regex matched text primary-foreground while looking for text primary. Pairs its fill and text CORRECTLY (primary + primary-foreground) - notable because Navigation Menu binds that same primary-foreground on a card fill where it is invisible. Size is one of the few genuinely tokenised dimensions (radius/16, /24, /32). GAP: no presence-dot colour recorded despite the record calling status dots intentional; asserted from the semantic families.

Badge._note: Implemented 9 Aug 2026. UNBLOCKED TWICE: wrongly flagged as stale by a regex error (text warning\b matched text warning-foreground), and its cap gap proved recoverable - 8 of 10 rows present, the two missing BOTH Destructive, pattern-completed from four tones sharing one shape (fill <tone> + text <tone>-foreground). DEFECT FLAGGED: Success binds text info-foreground, not success-foreground, reaching across to Info. Both resolve identically today so nothing is visibly wrong - exactly the condition that made a planned contrast fix a no-op once before. Transcribed as recorded (unlike Card and Navigation Menu where following the record gave INVISIBLE text). Badge is also what makes info-foreground legitimate: on a SOLID info fill it is correct, which identified Card use of it as the anomaly.

Breadcrumb._note: Implemented 9 Aug 2026. Figma models a FIXED three-level trail (Home/Parent/Current labels) because a design file cannot express a variable-length list; those three properties are one EXAMPLE of the array, not the API. Code takes items[]. GAPS: no token for the current page (everything binds muted-foreground, which would make the current page indistinguishable from its ancestors, so foreground is asserted), no separator token, no link/hover treatment. The collapse affordance is a real button with an accessible name, never an inert ellipsis - collapsing must not hide levels from assistive technology that a sighted user can reach.

Button._note: Implemented 9 Aug 2026 from LIVE BINDINGS via the Desktop Bridge. The longest-blocked component - 32 variants vs 8 description rows, with outline and ghost entirely missing. The read also proved THE DESCRIPTION FORMAT LOSES INFORMATION: live bindings carry spacing and stroke-weight tokens (space/1-5, space/2, space/3, space/4, space/2-25, stroke/1, stroke/2) that no ANATOMY block emits, plus primary-hover and accent-hover which appear in NO doc record anywhere. Every earlier no-spacing-token flag was wrong about the cause. GAP: disabled drops the outline border entirely, so a disabled outline button is indistinguishable from a disabled ghost one.

Button Group._note: Implemented 9 Aug 2026. Unblocked by the same regex correction. LAYOUT-ONLY: the record binds two tokens and primary-foreground is a LEAKED BINDING - the group has no fill, so the text colour FOR the primary fill sits on whatever is beneath; it almost certainly belongs to the nested Button instances. Identical in shape to Toggle Group stray accent-foreground and given identical treatment. ITS MEMBERS ARE BUTTONS AND BUTTON IS STILL BLOCKED (32 variants, 8 rows), so callers supply their own until then. Attached has no border/radius tokens so the shared-edge treatment is raw.

Calendar._note: Implemented 9 Aug 2026. FIVE STATES NAMED IN PROSE, ZERO IN TOKENS - the widest promise-to-binding gap in the build. The description ends 'Includes today, selected, range, disabled, and out-of-month' but tokensUsed is five CONTAINER tokens and not one day-state colour. All five asserted from precedent: selected=primary (Radio Group / Indicator), range=accent (Command/Toggle/menus), today=ring outline, disabled and out-of-month=muted-foreground. Six rows always rendered so the grid does not change height between months. Roving tabindex - one tabbable day, not 42. Days announce in full, not just the number. FIGMA OWES day-state bindings.

Card._note: Implemented 9 Aug 2026. THE ONLY COMPONENT WHOSE CODE DELIBERATELY DOES NOT MATCH ITS RECORD. Card.doc.json binds text to info-foreground, which is INVERTED relative to card-foreground (info-foreground is Light neutral/50 + Dark neutral/950; card-foreground is Light neutral/950 + Dark neutral/50). On a card fill that is near-white text on a white card in Light and near-black on near-black in Dark - contrast roughly 1:1, text invisible in BOTH modes. info-foreground is the light-on-dark pairing, correct for text on the SOLID info fill, which is how Badge uses it legitimately. Code binds card-foreground. Transcribing faithfully would ship a visible bug rather than a documentation inaccuracy. FIGMA OWES A REBIND; until then docs:adopt keeps re-importing the wrong token. Also transcribed-but-flagged: size/11 (smallest in the scale) for card text, and State=Interactive binding 2px primary, the same treatment Input uses for FOCUS, so an interactive card looks focused at rest.

Chart._note: Implemented 9 Aug 2026. THIS IS A FRAME, NOT A CHART. tokensUsed is five entries and EVERY ONE belongs to the container - no series colour, no axis, no gridline, no legend. The record's own name for itself is honest: 'Token-bound chart CONTAINER'. So it ships as a titled token-bound frame that a chart renders into; no data props, no series colours and no rendering, because supplying them would mean INVENTING A CATEGORICAL PALETTE, a substantial design-system decision not to be made by implication. Type carries no token delta and no rendering; passed through as a data attribute so a consuming chart can read it. FIGMA OWES a categorical series palette.

Checkbox._note: Implemented 9 Aug 2026. RECOVERED FROM THE 8-ROW CAP: 9 variants = Value(3) x State(3), 4 rows present; all three Disabled rows are IDENTICAL so Value carries no text delta (three observations, no exceptions) and the two missing Default rows match Unchecked/Default. The three missing Focused rows have zero observations but this record is text-only and focus is drawn on the box. THE BOX HAS NO TOKENS AT ALL, exactly as Switch track has none - and unlike Switch there is no sibling asset holding it. Asserted: input for the resting border, primary/primary-foreground for the checked fill. Indeterminate has NO HTML attribute - DOM property only, applied via ref.

Collapsible._note: Implemented 9 Aug 2026. Token-identical to Accordion, and unlike the Drawer/Sheet pair this is DEFENSIBLE: the Figma master draws one disclosure item, which is exactly what a Collapsible is, while an Accordion is a group of the same item. The records match because the design file draws one thing. Difference is real in code - one boolean vs items[]/openIds[]. Trigger deliberately NOT wrapped in a heading: a lone Collapsible usually sits inside content that already has one.

Command._note: Implemented 9 Aug 2026. This asset is one ITEM, not the palette (Command Panel is separate and not in this build). The record is precise: Selected=True is the HIGHLIGHTED option - the active descendant, not a chosen value; a command palette selects nothing, it runs things. So focus never lands here: it stays in the search input which points via aria-activedescendant, hence the id prop. Shortcut is aria-hidden - screen readers announce the label and the glyphs would read as punctuation. No shortcut token (muted asserted) and no disabled treatment exists.

Data Table._note: Implemented 9 Aug 2026. State=Populated|Empty is NOT a prop: a populated data table with no rows contradicts itself, so the state is derived from whether there is anything to show - same move as Progress's Type and Card's media. THIS COMPOSITION NAMES FOUR COMPONENTS AND ONE IS BLOCKED: the record says 'built from Input, Button, Table, and Pagination'; Input, Table and Pagination are all built but BUTTON IS NOT (32 variants, 8 rows). The toolbar is therefore a SLOT left to the caller rather than pre-composed with a Button that does not exist. GAP: the empty state changes only the type size - no muted colour, no distinct treatment - and there is no loading or error state at all.

Date Picker._note: Implemented 9 Aug 2026 from LIVE BINDINGS. Its read also gave THE AUTHORITATIVE DAY STATES that Calendar names in prose and binds nowhere: four of five Calendar assertions were CORRECT; today is a primary STROKE not a ring outline, and calendar.tsx was corrected. GAP against the archetype: the asset records only a button trigger, so typing a date is not implemented.

Dialog._note: Implemented 9 Aug 2026 on the native <dialog> element via the shared internal components/modal-surface.tsx. showModal() supplies the focus trap, Escape, top layer and ::backdrop from the platform, following the NativeSelect precedent. children/footer are SLOTS not typed props, per the record's instruction that embedded copy must not be generated as a public code prop until engineering API review. GAPS: Size has no token backing (there are NO width or container tokens anywhere in the file - every size/* variable is a type size), and the backdrop has no token.

Drawer._note: Implemented 9 Aug 2026. See the Sheet note - the two are indistinguishable in the design file.

Dropdown Menu._note: Implemented 9 Aug 2026. Correct surface pairing (popover + popover-foreground). Type and Density BOTH carry no token delta - Type describes what is inside rather than how the container looks, and Density is the fourth component in this system with no spacing token, so padding is raw. Primary item label / Primary shortcut are example content not API, same pattern as Table row labels and Breadcrumb levels.

Dropdown Menu / Checkbox Item._note: Implemented 9 Aug 2026. RECOVERED FROM THE CAP: all three Highlighted rows bind identical tokens so Value is provably inert and the two missing Default rows match Unchecked/Default. AND THAT INERTNESS IS ITSELF THE DEFECT, same as the radio item: there is NO RECORDED WAY to tell a checked item from an unchecked one. For a multi-select control that is the state that must be visible, so an indicator is asserted; aria-checked carries it correctly so this is a sighted-user gap. The icon slot and the indicator compete for the leading position and the indicator wins when checked - forced by the missing token, not a design choice.

Dropdown Menu / Content._note: Implemented 9 Aug 2026 from LIVE BINDINGS. Side and Align carry NO colour delta - 24 variants collapse to THREE sets differing only by the Arrow node. Purely geometric axes, which could not have been guessed from 1 of 24 rows.

Dropdown Menu / Item._note: Implemented 9 Aug 2026. RECOVERED FROM THE CAP: 12 variants = Tone(2) x State(3) x Inset(2), 8 rows present. Inset is PROVABLY INERT - all three pairs present bind identical tokens. The two Default/Disabled gaps rest on a WEAKER single-observation inference (Destructive/Disabled is identical to Destructive/Default), consistent with this family recording no disabled tokens anywhere; flagged as weaker than the Inset proof. Both Show icon and Show shortcut are slot-toggles so the booleans disappear. FLAGGED: destructive highlighted keeps destructive text on an accent fill - deliberate in the record but a pairing the token system does not define, so contrast is unverified.

Dropdown Menu / Label._note: Implemented 9 Aug 2026. role=presentation and non-focusable per the record, so arrow-key navigation skips it - a label announced as an item is a dead end. GAP: it binds full-strength popover-foreground, the SAME colour as the items it labels, so a label looks exactly like the things beneath it; muted-foreground would be the usual treatment. Inset changes padding only and no spacing token is recorded.

Dropdown Menu / Radio Item._note: Implemented 9 Aug 2026. THE CHECKED STATE HAS NO RECORDED VISUAL: both Checked rows in the record are Highlighted rows and are identical to the unchecked highlighted row, so there is no recorded way to tell a checked radio item from an unchecked one. For an exclusive-choice control that is the one state that must be visible, so a check indicator is ASSERTED, not transcribed. aria-checked carries it correctly either way, so this is a sighted-user gap only. FIGMA OWES a checked indicator. The Show icon boolean collapsed into the nullable icon slot per the map kind: slot-toggle.

Dropdown Menu / Sub Content._note: Implemented 9 Aug 2026. Identical tokens to Dropdown Menu, which is correct - a submenu is the same surface. Neither Side nor Align carries a token delta; both are pure geometry. The `side` vocabulary (opens to the left/right OF THE TRIGGER) is correct here, unlike on Sheet where the surface attaches to the viewport. Placement is not collision-aware, same limitation as Popover.

Dropdown Menu / Sub Trigger._note: Implemented 9 Aug 2026. Inset is PROVABLY INERT - both Inset pairs present (Open and Highlighted) bind identical tokens, the same reasoning that recovered Table / Row. GAP: Open and Highlighted bind IDENTICAL tokens (accent fill, accent-foreground text), so a sub trigger looks the same whether its submenu is open or merely hovered - no feedback that it opened. No submenu indicator token either. Right Arrow opens and moves in, Left closes and returns; flips in RTL.

Dropdown Menu / Trigger._note: Implemented 9 Aug 2026. NOTE THE CONTRAST WITH NativeSelect: both maps annotate State with a `controlled` open state. There it was deliberately NOT emitted because a native select menu is platform-owned and unobservable; here the menu is ours, can be opened programmatically, and aria-expanded needs it. Same annotation, opposite conclusion - the difference is who owns the popup. GAPS: avatar/closed binds accent-foreground with NO fill (that token is the text colour FOR the accent fill, so it sits on whatever is beneath - same class as Card, far less severe); disabled changes text only with no fill change, unlike every other disabled control here; no disabled variant exists for the avatar type.

Field._note: Implemented 9 Aug 2026. Owns the accessibility wiring (generates id, binds label-for/aria-describedby/aria-invalid) via a render prop rather than cloneElement, so injected props are type-checked at the call site. The Figma Value property has NO code equivalent — the control is a child, so Field owning a value would be a competing source of truth. KNOWN CONFLICT: Input/Textarea/NativeSelect each render their own errorMessage, so inside a Field the error must be passed to Field, not the control, or you get two messages and two live regions. KNOWN INCONSISTENCY, recorded not resolved: Field uses aria-live=polite per its record; Input uses role=alert. Both cannot be right; moving the three shipped controls needs its own review.

Hover Card._note: Implemented 9 Aug 2026. Opens on focus as well as hover: the record is explicit that it must be reachable on keyboard focus or its content must exist elsewhere, since hover alone excludes keyboard and touch users. closeDelay lets the pointer travel from trigger into the card without it vanishing. Density is not just spacing - the record ties detailed density to supporting metadata, so density sets spacing and meta is the content it makes room for; meta without detailed renders nothing.

Label._note: Implemented 9 Aug 2026. Two deliberate divergences from figma.map.json, both in Table 2: State is a boolean not a two-value enum (the record's own governance rule keeps visual State axes as story states, and every other control here uses disabled: boolean); and Type has THREE code states because most labels carry no marker at all and Figma has no variant for that, which the record's own dont requires. The marker is aria-hidden and deliberately not tinted destructive — tokensUsed records no marker colour.

Native Select._note: Implemented 9 Aug 2026 from docs/components/native-select.md. The map lists controlled: ["open"] but Open was deliberately NOT emitted as a prop: a native select menu is platform-owned, cannot be opened programmatically, and Open binds tokens identical to Focus because the control is always focused while its menu is up. appearance-none is deliberately NOT set, so the platform draws its own indicator — tokensUsed carries no chevron colour and suppressing it would mean inventing a token that does not exist. Rendered and built in Storybook; not yet visually reviewed.

Navigation Menu._note: Implemented 9 Aug 2026. THE SECOND COMPONENT WHOSE CODE DELIBERATELY DIVERGES FROM ITS RECORD. It binds fill card + text primary-foreground; primary-foreground is blue/50 (near-white) in BOTH modes, so on a white card in Light the text is INVISIBLE. Dark survives, so this is a light-mode-only failure, narrower than Card which broke in both. Code binds foreground. Same cause as Card: a *-foreground token paired with a fill it does not belong to. FIGMA OWES A REBIND. Also flagged: compact/open binds accent-foreground with no accent fill - the fourth component with that shape (Sidebar collapsed, Dropdown Menu / Trigger avatar, Popover / Trigger).

Pagination._note: Implemented 9 Aug 2026. Viewport is kind: responsive-fixture and would normally be dropped (it was for Table / Container and Sidebar) - THIS IS THE EXCEPTION, because the record describes a STRUCTURAL difference not a breakpoint: 'Desktop exposes page numbers; Compact uses a concise page summary.' Different content, not the same content reflowed. State=Disabled is NOT a prop: previous is disabled at page 1 and next at the last page, which is arithmetic, and a prop would let a caller contradict it. GAP: three tokens and NO state distinctions at all - no current page, no disabled, no hover, no focus, no radius; all asserted from convention.

Popover._note: Implemented 9 Aug 2026. Uses the CORRECT surface pairing (popover fill + popover-foreground text) - worth noting against Dialog which binds plain foreground on a card fill, and Card whose text token is outright wrong. Size has no width token (same gap as Dialog). PLACEMENT IS NOT COLLISION-AWARE: places on the requested side and stays there; flipping needs a positioning library, out of scope for a token-level component and recorded rather than half-built. The modal prop implements the record line exactly: a popover holding a form should trap focus, a non-modal one should not.

Popover / Arrow._note: Implemented 9 Aug 2026 from LIVE BINDINGS - third child-node record. popover fill + border stroke on all four sides; Side is pure geometry. Also fills the arrow-token gap popover.md had flagged.

Popover / Backdrop._note: Implemented 9 Aug 2026. THE ONLY SCRIM TOKEN IN THE SYSTEM AND IT IS THE WRONG KIND. Binds fill foreground, which is neutral/950 Light and neutral/50 Dark - it INVERTS, giving a near-black scrim in Light (right) and a near-WHITE scrim in Dark (wrong). Dialog/Drawer/Sheet/AlertDialog record no backdrop token at all, which is why modal-surface.tsx falls back to raw black/50. So there is no correct scrim token anywhere. Applied as recorded because unlike Card it produces a visible functioning backdrop and deviating would mean inventing; FIGMA OWES an overlay/scrim token, which would close five gaps at once.

Popover / Close._note: Implemented 9 Aug 2026. Defaults label to Close rather than requiring it, unlike TableActionTrigger where the name must identify a row - here Close genuinely is right almost every time and a required prop everyone fills identically is friction not safety. Binds radius/7, a half-step ramp member and the only component that uses it; written as an explicit calc so it can never degrade to a raw pixel value. No disabled tokens and no icon colour recorded.

Popover / Content._note: Implemented 9 Aug 2026 from LIVE BINDINGS. 48 variants collapse to THREE sets. AND THE ACTION LINK BINDS primary-readable - one of the three rebind tokens, appearing in no description anywhere. That is the clearest single proof that the bindings are current while the descriptions are stale.

Popover / Root Composition._note: DELIBERATELY NOT BOUND TO CODE, same treatment as Table / Root Composition: its Pattern axis is kind: story-only (Storybook story, never a prop). Its four patterns - Basic, Align, Form, RTL - ship as stories in components/popover.stories.tsx.

Popover / Trigger._note: Implemented 9 Aug 2026. RECOVERED FROM THE CAP: 10 variants = Type(button|rTL) x State(5), 8 rows present. Every rTL row carries the SAME single delta and nothing else (type size/12) - three rows, one token, no exceptions - so the Type axis changes only the type size and the two missing rTL rows are their Button counterparts at size/12. NOTE: rTL is NOT a visual variant at all; direction is a document concern (dir=rtl plus logical properties), never a prop, so what the axis really documents is that RTL renders one type step smaller. FLAGGED: Open and Hover bind identical tokens so the trigger looks the same open or hovered - same gap as Dropdown Menu / Sub Trigger.

Popover / Viewport._note: Implemented 9 Aug 2026. THIS WAS THE LAST UNRESOLVED DOC BLOCK IN THE SYSTEM - six variant meanings left deliberately owed because the side axis already holds top/right/bottom/left for placement and guessing would have put a wrong meaning in six blocks. Its own description settled it without a Figma query: direction is an ACTIVATION direction (data-activation-direction), not placement, and current/previous are the incoming and outgoing halves of a transition. Vocabulary added on that evidence; the system now has ZERO owed doc blocks. State deliberately did NOT become an enum: both halves render at once during a transition and an enum could only show one.

Progress._note: Implemented 9 Aug 2026. tokensUsed is muted and radius/lg - two entries, BOTH belonging to the track. The filled portion, the only part that conveys progress, has NO colour recorded; asserted as primary on the Radio Group / Indicator precedent. `Type` deliberately did NOT become an enum: a determinate bar with no value is meaningless and an indeterminate one with a value contradicts itself, so deriving the type from value's presence makes the invalid pair unrepresentable - the same move as Card's media slot. Indeterminate OMITS aria-valuenow, which is precisely what tells assistive tech the value is unknown. Also flagged: radius/lg on a thin bar reads as nearly square; radius/full would be usual.

Radio Group._note: Implemented 9 Aug 2026. Same shape of gap as Switch: tokensUsed is three TEXT tokens; the outer circle lives on Radio Group / Root, which is BLOCKED (24 variants). The circle border is ASSERTED as input. Unlike Switch the SELECTED half is real - Radio Group / Indicator records fill primary - so only the ring is asserted, not the state colour. Figma models ONE option; a group has N, so items[] plus a single group-level `value` string, which makes two selected items unrepresentable by construction. fieldset+legend, not a wrapper label. Arrow keys move AND select in one step, which differs from ToggleGroup.

Radio Group / Field Composition._note: DELIBERATELY NOT BOUND TO CODE: kind: story-only, same as Switch / Field Composition. Its seven patterns ship as stories.

Radio Group / Indicator._note: Implemented 9 Aug 2026. THE ONE RECORDED PIECE OF THE RADIO'S SELECTED STATE (fill primary + radius/full), and the precedent that made Switch's track and Progress's bar assertions defensible - primary is demonstrably this system's checked-state colour. forceMount has no Figma property but is required by the record's prose: runtime may force-mount for animation or measurement; unmounting kills an exit animation and makes the element unmeasurable. Force-mounted and unchecked means hidden from sight AND assistive technology, not merely transparent.

Radio Group / Item._note: Implemented 9 Aug 2026 from LIVE BINDINGS. CONFIRMS the asserted input resting border. Same disabled-indistinguishable defect as Switch / Root.

Radio Group / Root._note: Implemented 9 Aug 2026 from LIVE BINDINGS. Orientation carries NO colour delta - 24 variants collapse to 9 distinct sets. Disabled changes only the LABELS, leaving circles at full strength. Invalid marks EVERY item destructive including unchecked ones.

Scroll Area._note: Implemented 9 Aug 2026. The record's own description promises anatomy it does not bind: 'visible track and thumb anatomy', but tokensUsed is five entries all belonging to the viewport container. Rather than invent two colours the NATIVE SCROLLBAR IS KEPT - the same decision, for the same reason, as NativeSelect's chevron, and it keeps native scroll behaviour intact. The focusable+named region is the important part: a region that scrolls but cannot be focused is UNREACHABLE BY KEYBOARD, the most common failure of custom scroll areas.

Segmented Tab._note: Implemented 9 Aug 2026. The item half of Tabs. Note the inversion: the SELECTED tab takes the lighter card fill and lifts out of the muted track rather than being highlighted, which only reads correctly inside the container. The map types Selected as a false|true string union; emitted as a real boolean. Focus ring is asserted from the record’s own prose ("focus remains visually distinguishable using the shared ring treatment") rather than transcribed from a binding. No disabled variant exists.

Separator._note: Implemented 9 Aug 2026. decorative has no Figma property and must exist: the record splits the component semantically with no visual difference, so Figma cannot express it. Defaults to decorative. A semantic vertical separator also sets aria-orientation, because role=separator implies horizontal.

Sheet._note: Implemented 9 Aug 2026. DRAWER AND SHEET ARE IDENTICAL IN EVERY RECORDED RESPECT: same tokensUsed, same state rows, same variant count, same props, same accessibility. The ONLY difference is the placement axis name (Drawer=Placement, Sheet=Side) with the same two values. The distinction exists only as prose. Both built as specified rather than merged because collapsing them is a design decision; they share modal-surface.tsx so they cannot drift further. UNRESOLVED - worth deciding: give them a real visual difference, or collapse them.

Sidebar._note: Implemented 9 Aug 2026. Viewport is kind: responsive-fixture so NOT a prop, same as Table / Container. GAP: collapsed switches text to sidebar-accent-foreground with NO accent fill - that token is the foreground FOR sidebar-accent, so it sits on plain sidebar; same class of mismatch as Dropdown Menu / Trigger avatar. No width tokens exist anywhere in the file so both widths are raw.

Sidebar Navigation Item._note: Implemented 9 Aug 2026. THE BEST-BEHAVED COLOUR RECORD IN THE SYSTEM: dedicated sidebar-* family throughout, with fill and matching foreground correctly paired (sidebar-accent + sidebar-accent-foreground). Compare Card (info-foreground on a card fill) and Dialog (plain foreground on card). Active is derived from the route, never set by hand. Collapsed keeps the label in the DOM visually hidden so the item keeps its accessible name. GAPS: no hover/focus tokens, no height token despite the record calling fixed height intentional.

Skeleton._note: Implemented 9 Aug 2026 from LIVE BINDINGS - another child-node record. EVERY shape in EVERY variant binds muted; the four types differ only in which shapes exist.

Slider._note: Implemented 9 Aug 2026 from LIVE BINDINGS - a no-root-level-bindings record whose tokens all live on Track/Range/Thumb children. Complete, consistent contract: every state distinguishable, unlike several root-level records.

Switch._note: Implemented 9 Aug 2026. THIS ASSET RECORDS THE LABEL, NOT THE SWITCH: its entire tokensUsed is foreground / muted-foreground / size/14 - three TEXT tokens and nothing else. No track fill, no checked colour, no border. Switch / Thumb gives the thumb (card + radius/full) and SWITCH / ROOT, WHICH HOLDS THE TRACK, IS BLOCKED by the 8-row cap (24 variants). The track is ASSERTED as primary (checked) / input (unchecked) on the strongest precedent available: Radio Group / Indicator binds fill primary for its checked indicator, so primary is this system's checked-state colour. THIS IS THE LARGEST ASSERTION IN THE BUILD - re-verify when Switch / Root is readable. role=switch with aria-checked; Space toggles and Enter does not, which is the switch convention and differs from Toggle.

Switch / Field Composition._note: DELIBERATELY NOT BOUND TO CODE: its Pattern axis is kind: story-only ("Storybook story, never a prop"), same treatment as the Table and Popover root compositions. Its seven patterns ship as stories in components/switch.stories.tsx.

Switch / Root._note: Implemented 9 Aug 2026 from LIVE BINDINGS. CONFIRMS the assertion made in switch.tsx: input unchecked, primary checked. DEFECT: Disabled and ReadOnly bind EXACTLY the same tokens as Default, so a disabled switch is visually indistinguishable from an operable one - a real accessibility problem, not cosmetic. Same pattern confirmed on Radio Group / Item.

Switch / Thumb._note: Implemented 9 Aug 2026. The record states both its axes are inherited: "Size follows the Root size; disabled styling is inherited from the Root state", so neither carries a token delta and none is applied. radius/full is the correct token for a circle - no raw 9999px. Size has no dimension token, so both sizes are raw.

Table._note: Implemented 9 Aug 2026. Figma's Selection axis is NOT a prop: selection belongs to a ROW (Table / Row carries State=Selected with a real accent fill), so a table-level selection prop would be a second source of truth. First/Second row label are example content, not API - same pattern as Breadcrumb's three fixed labels. DENSITY CARRIES NO TOKEN DELTA anywhere in this family, verified not assumed: Table / Row shows three Compact/Comfortable pairs and all three bind identical tokens, so row height is raw padding.

Table / Action Trigger._note: Implemented 9 Aug 2026. `label` is REQUIRED in the type on purpose: the record's accessibility contract demands 'a programmatic accessible name that identifies the action context (for example, Open row actions)', and making it optional would make it forgettable. GAPS: no disabled tokens and no icon colour are recorded; shared conventions asserted.

Table / Caption._note: Implemented 9 Aug 2026. The record: 'Position is visual; code should preserve caption semantics and reading order.' A <caption> must be the FIRST CHILD of <table> wherever it appears, so bottom placement uses caption-side and never DOM reordering - moving it would break the naming relationship.

Table / Cell._note: Implemented 9 Aug 2026. EMPHASIS CHANGES COLOUR, NOT WEIGHT, despite its name and despite the shared vocabulary calling it 'heavier weight'. The record binds foreground vs muted-foreground and no weight token; transcribed as bound, not as named. CONSEQUENCE WORTH REVIEWING: a DEFAULT cell is muted-foreground, so ordinary table data renders muted and only 'strong' cells get full contrast - backwards from the usual convention, and it affects every cell in every table.

Table / Container._note: Implemented 9 Aug 2026. Figma's Viewport axis is kind: responsive-fixture - the map itself says 'Not a prop unless code deliberately exposes one' - so overflow is plain CSS and takes no input. The scroll region is focusable AND named, because a region that scrolls but cannot be focused is unreachable by keyboard. GAP: the record binds size/10 (smallest in the file) on a wrapper that renders no text of its own, almost certainly inherited from a nested example; deliberately not applied.

Table / Head._note: Implemented 9 Aug 2026. `scope` has no Figma property but is required by the record's own prose ('use scope/row-header semantics in code where applicable'); a th without scope is ambiguous in any table with both row and column headers. GAP: no fill is recorded on the head cell - the header band's muted fill lives on Table / Row (Type=Header) - so TableHead used outside a header row would be transparent.

Table / Root Composition._note: DELIBERATELY NOT BOUND TO CODE. Its map entry has no real properties - Pattern is kind: story-only ("Storybook story, never a prop") and Viewport is kind: responsive-fixture. It is a set of composition examples, so it ships as the four stories in components/table.stories.tsx (Basic, Footer, Actions, RTL). Binding it would claim it is a component.

Table / Row._note: Implemented 9 Aug 2026. RECOVERED FROM THE 8-ROW CAP BY INFERENCE, not guesswork. 10 variants, 8 rows shown; the two missing are Header/Comfortable and Footer/Comfortable. Every Compact/Comfortable pair that IS present binds identical tokens (three pairs, three matches), so Density is proven inert in this record and the absent rows carry their Compact twins tokens. This does NOT generalise - it works because the missing rows sit on an axis proven inert by the rows that survived; Popover / Content shows 1 of 48 and stays blocked. ASSERTED: recorded hover binds only text, identical to resting, so a muted tint is added rather than transcribed. No focus token for a selectable row either.

Tabs._note: Implemented 9 Aug 2026. TABS AND SEGMENTED TAB ARE TWO HALVES OF ONE CONTROL. Tabs binds only a container fill (muted) and has NO selected-state treatment at all; Segmented Tab binds exactly that treatment and no container. Segmented Tab’s own description confirms it: "Place instances inside a secondary-colored segmented-control container." Neither is complete alone, so Tabs renders SegmentedTab items. Neither Orientation nor Density carries a token delta, so both are layout-only and Density uses raw padding (no spacing token is recorded). No focus token either; the shared ring is asserted.

Textarea._note: Implemented 9 Aug 2026 from docs/components/textarea.md, which was transcribed rather than authored. Shares Input's visual contract token-for-token, so Input's three resolved build blockers were inherited, not re-decided. Focus is keyed on focus-visible: directly rather than has-[:focus-visible] because there is no wrapper — no slots means the focusable and bordered element are the same node. resize-none enforces the record's fixed-viewport sizing policy. The character counter is deliberately NOT a live region: polite announcement per keystroke is noise, so it is linked via aria-describedby and read on focus. Rendered and built in Storybook; not yet visually reviewed.

Toggle._note: Implemented 9 Aug 2026. THE RECORD’S ACCESSIBILITY CONTRACT WAS WRONG and was fixed: Toggle was mapped to the `choice` archetype, which told it to expose state via aria-checked and referenced radio-group arrow keys. A toggle button is the W3C APG Toggle Button pattern - aria-pressed, and both Space and Enter activate. Added a `togglebutton` archetype and remapped Toggle + Toggle Group, then re-enriched. THREE RECORDED ODDITIES, transcribed rather than corrected: (1) Pressed+hover binds the SAME tokens as pressed at rest, so a pressed toggle gives no hover feedback; (2) it binds radius/md where every other control in the system binds radius/lg; (3) Pressed+disabled loses the pressed state entirely and renders identically to unpressed+disabled - aria-pressed still reports it so assistive tech is correct, but a sighted user cannot tell. 8 variants is exactly at the 8-row cap, so nothing is truncated.

Toggle Group._note: Implemented 9 Aug 2026. THE RECORD IS ALMOST EMPTY - one state row and two tokens (accent-foreground, size/14) for four variants, the thinnest of any component built so far. And accent-foreground looks like a stray binding: it is the foreground for the accent fill, but the group binds no fill of its own, so it is a foreground token with nothing to sit on. The items (Toggle) already carry accent/accent-foreground for their pressed state. Implemented as a LAYOUT-ONLY container with each Toggle owning its appearance, which is what the tokens actually support. Figma owes either a real container treatment or the removal of that binding. role=group NOT radiogroup even in single mode, since members are toggle buttons; single mode has no must-have-one guard because all members may legitimately be off when they are actions.

Tooltip._note: Implemented 9 Aug 2026. label is deliberately a STRING not a ReactNode - everywhere else a content property was widened to a node, but the record calls this brief non-interactive and a node slot invites buttons and links into a surface unreachable by keyboard and invisible on touch. The narrow type is the guardrail. The fill/text inversion (foreground fill + card text) is CORRECT and deliberate; note it is the same foreground token that is wrong as a backdrop - as a fill behind short text it inverts correctly, as a full-screen scrim it inverts backwards.
